fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance so responders can identify the property quickly from the road.
• Mark the single driveway entrance clearly, as it is the only access point to the property.
• Keep the access drive clear of parked vehicles so emergency apparatus can reach both structures.
• Create a designated turnaround or pull-out area near the detached structure to allow emergency vehicles to reverse direction without backing the full length of the driveway.
• Trim dense vegetation along the access drive to maintain clear passage for emergency vehicles on both sides.
• Cut back vegetation growing close to both the main residence and the detached structure so responders can move around the buildings without obstruction.
• Keep the walkway between the main residence and detached structure clear so responders can move between the two buildings on foot.
• Mark or identify the detached structure with a visible label or number so arriving responders can distinguish it from the main residence.
• Keep the patio area clear of stored items so responders can use it as a staging or working area if needed.
• Cut back any dense vegetation that blocks sightlines from the access drive to either structure so responders can assess both buildings on approach.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Remove or thin shrubs and brush that are growing directly against or within a few feet of the structure on all sides.
• Thin the tree clusters near the structure to create open space between individual trees and between the trees and the structure.
• Remove low-hanging branches from scattered trees close to the structure so flames cannot climb from ground vegetation up into the tree canopy.
• Cut back and thin brush in the brush area closest to the structure to reduce the concentration of flammable plant material near the building.
• Separate scattered shrubs near the structure by removing some and spacing remaining plants so they are not touching or forming a continuous line toward the building.
• Clear vegetation growing along both sides of the driveway to maintain an open travel lane for vehicles including emergency equipment.
• Trim overhanging branches along the driveway so they do not block passage or drop debris onto the roadway.
• Keep the driveway surface clear of fallen branches, dead leaves, and plant debris that accumulate along the edges.
• Maintain a visible, unobstructed path around the exterior of the structure by keeping vegetation cut back far enough for a person to walk freely on all sides.
• Because there is only one access route, keep it passable at all times and remove any vegetation that narrows or partially blocks entry or exit.
